0.1 This Indian

FOREWORD

Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 30 November 1985, after the draft finalized by the Ceramicware Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council.

0.2 The Committee, while reviewing IS:3972-1968*, decided to publish it in two parts. Part 1 deals with production of specimen for testing, in two sections, namely, Section 1 Enamelled sheet steel, and Section 2 Enamelled cast iron. Part 2 deals with various test methods applicable to vitreous enamelled sheet, and vitreous enamelled cast iron, The Committee also decided that Part 2 shall have various sections and each section would deal with a particular test method. 0.3 In the preparation of this standard ( Part 2/Set 2 ) assistance has been derived from the following standards issued by International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ). ISO/DIS-8289 Vitreous and porcelain detecting and locating defects. enamels low voltage test for

180/2746-1973 Vitreous and porcelain enamels - Enamelled .articles for service under highly corrosive condition-high voltage test. 0.4 in reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS:2-1960t.
*Methods of test.for vitreous enamelware. tRules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ).

IS : 3972 ( Part S/See 2 ) - 1985
1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the methods of test for detecting and locating defects in vitreous enamelled sheet steel and vitreous enamelled cast iron articles using a low and high voltage.
NOTE 1 -The low voltage test is not intended as an alternative to high .voltage test, but is a non-destructive test method for detecting defects which extend down to the metal base and weak spots in the enamel layer. NOTE2 -The purpose of the high voltage test is to detect and locate defectsdwhich extend down to the metal base, and weak spots in the enamel layer, that is, those areas of the enamel laver where Its thickness falls below the required value determined by the application of high voltage, because of blistfrs, foreign body inclusions, spalling or cracks.

2. TERMINOLOGY

2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS: 2717-1979*, in addition to the following, shall apply. 2.1 Defects - Pores, tears, cracks or spalls, which penetrate metal.
2.2 Weak Spots -

to the base

Those areas of the enamel layer where its thickness falls below the required value determined by the application of high voltage, because of blisters, foreign body inclusions, spalling or cracks. 3. TEST SPECIMENS

3.1 The test specimens may be commercial

special preparation

LOCATING

4.0 Principle - Testing is carried out with low voltage, contact being made with the defect by means of an electrolyte (conductive fluid). Readings indicating the presence of a fault may be made with an electrical measuring instrument or acoustically with headphones. Additionally, the defects may be made visible by colour effects.

4.1 Test Fluid 4.1.1 Dissolve 3 & 0.5 g of sodium chloride in 100 ml of water and add two drops of a liquid detergent. Jf the defects are to be made visible by means of a colour effect, add about 1 ml of 0.5 percent (m/m ) phenolphthalein ethanolic solution.
*Glossary of terms ( first revision ). relating to vitreous enamelware and ceramic-metal systems

4

IS : 3972 ( Part 2/Set 2 ) - 1985
&2 Apparatus 4.2.1 Power Source 4.2.1.1 Testing with direct current - Use a 9 V battery, capable of being adjusted in the range 0 to 9 V. A transistor radio battery 6 F 100 complying with the requirements of IS : 2576-1975* is suitable.

4.2.1.2 Testing with alternating current - An alternating voltage the amplitude of which can be infinitely adjusted between 0 V and the maximum value about 5 V.
NOTE - The signal frequency superimposed the audio range (600 to 900 Hz). on the alternating

voltage lies within

4.3 Test Electrode
4.3.1 The test electrode consists of a plastics sponge, made of cellulose or similar material, soaked with the test fluid ( 4.1). Its size will depend on the desired accuracy of location and it is conductively connected, via a metal lead, to the positive pole of the apparatus.

4.3.2 For quick testing ( coarse scanning) of large' enamelled surfaces, test electrodes with an area up to 100 cm8 are suitable; for the accurate location of defects, test electrodes with an ,area of a maximum of 1 cm9 are required.
NOTE - A large test electrode suitable for quick teiting may also be used for locating defects-possibly using an increased sensitivity-if the enamelled surface is only touched by an edge of the test electrode.

4.4 Means of Indicating the Defects 4.4.1 If direct current is used, the current flow through the defects may be detected by means of a short circuit proof microammeter. 4.4.2 If alternating current is used, the current flowing through the defects may be detected as an acoustic signal by means of headphones. The intensity ( sound level ) of the signal depends on the magnitude of the current flowing through the defects. Other methods of indication may also be used. 4.5 Procedure 4.5.1 Connect the electrically conductive base metal of the article to be tested to one pole ( negative in the case of direct current) of the power source ( 4.2.1). l Specificationfor dry batteries for transistor radio receivers( jrst revision ).
5

IS : 3972 ( Part Z/Set 2 ) - 1985 4.5.2 Connect the test electrode (sponge) ( 4.3 ) to the other pole in the case of direct current ) of the power source ( 4.2.1). Soak the test electrode ( 4.3 ) in the test fluid until it is dripping wet and.move it over the enamel surface at a speed not exceeding 0.2 metrelsecond.
( positive

4.5.3 Start the test using a voltage around the mid-point of the selected range. Defects permit a current to flow whose magnitude depends on the area of the defect and the distance between the defect and the test electrode. Increase the voltage if no reading is obtained. 4.5.4 By varying the test voltage, the sensitivity of the test is adjusted so that when measuring with direct current, the pointer of the microammeter swings within the indicated range and when measuring with alternating ( see Notes 1 and 2 in 4.5.5 ). voltage, the sound level is acceptable. 4.5.5 If it is intended to make the defects visible, ensure that a pool of the test fluid remains on the area under test or that the test specimen is wetted with the test fluid. When testing with direct current (4.2.1.1), an intense red colour will develop in the test fluid in the vicinity of the defects after about 3 to 15 seconds.
NOTE 1 -It is emphasized that it is not the magnitude of the reading of interest but its change due to the change in position of the test electrode. that is

NOTE 2 - Testing with alternating current ( 4.2.1.2 ), in addition to being more sensitive, enables the person carrying out the test to concentrate more fully on the article to be tested. Where there are numerous defects within the wetted testing area. However, the intensity ( sound level ) depends to a large extent on the distance of the teskelectrode from the neighbouring defect. It is therefore possible to locate defects which are not very far ( 10 mm and more ) from large areas of defects ( for example, at the rim ).

4.6 Test Report 4.6.1 The test report shall include the following information: a) identification of the article tested; b) the number and positions of defects; and c) the d&cription of the defects, where appropriate. 5. HIGH VOLTAGE TEST FOR DETECTING AND LOCATING DEFECTS 5.0 Principle 5.0.1 High voltage testing is carried out with dc voltage above 2 kV by passing a positive electrode over the enamel surface; the high voltage generator indicates defects and weak spots by a spark discharge and a simultaneous optical and/or acoustic signal. 6

IS : 3972 ( Part 2/$ec 2) - 1985 5.1 Apparatus 5.1.1 High Voltage Tester - To deliver dc voltage above 2 kV corresponding to the testing voltage ( 5.2.2) and adjustable with the tolerances f 5 percent. The total internal resistance shall be high enough to give the short-circuit current of the generator an arithmetical mean from 2 to 3 mA maximum. The peak value of the current during the spark discharge must be between IO and 50 mA maximum an amount of charge per impulse may be 25~ C maximum.

The negative pole of the generator shall be earthed and the positive pole shall be connected to the test electrode by a screened high voltage capable of suitable length. 5.1.2 Test Electrode - The test electrodes consist of an insulated handpiece and a brush holder made of metal wire for the test brush. The latter shall be constructed in such a way that it is completely unaffected by the spark discharge and shall be able to cover as large area as possible when sweeping the enamel surface. The hand-piece ,shall be provided externally with an earthed metal cover. A protective resistor shall be arranged between the hand-piece and the test brush to limit the peak current value ( IO to 50 mA maximum) during the electric spark discharge. This resistor shall be constructed in such a way that racking due to deposits of dirt reducing its value or the formation of an arc during the operation is not possible. 5.1.3 Voltage Control and Indication of Defects and Weak Areas - The test voltage sh&ll be measured accurately to f 5 percent directly behind the protective resistor of,the hand-piece. A device shall be provided which will give a clear option and/or acoustic signal at each spark discharge. 5.2 Procedure 5.2.1 The surface of the enamel layer under test shall be dry and free from impurities. The enamel layer shall have a temperature at 30�C maximum. The metallic base material shall be earthed. 5.2.2 Apply the test voltage by taking into account enamelled article, bearing in mind the dielectric strength ness of the enamel for an example as shown in Fig. 1. It at least l-5 times the break-down voltage for a layer of thickness. 7 end-use of the and layer thickshall amount to air of the same

If the voltage at the brush falls by more than 10 percent without a spark discharge occurring, investigate and remove the cause ( see 5.2.1). Defects and weak spots are indicated by a visible spark and simultaneously by an optical and/or acoustic signal. Wherever a spark discharge occurs on the enamel surface it means a contact point and indicates the position of a defect or weak spot. 8
